title: Latency slices & heatmap dashboard — planning notes for token-serving observability
content:
Summary:
This is an informal planning doc for a new observability surface focused on latency 'slices' and a heatmap-style dashboard for token-serving latency. The goal is to give product and infra teams a way to quickly see where time is spent across the lifecycle of a request (enqueue/batching/compute/post-process) and to surface hotspots by token position and model micro-operation.

Why now:
- We routinely see tail-latency regressions that are hard to attribute to queueing vs compute vs post-processing.
- Existing latency graphs (p50/p90/p99 by route) lack dimensionality: they don’t show per-token trends or phase breakdowns.
- Customers ask for token-level heatmaps (sequence position vs latency) to debug streaming regressions.

High-level goals:
- Define a compact set of metrics (and labels) that let us slice latency by phase, model, route, deployment_type, priority, and token_position.
- Provide 2 dashboards: (1) latency-slice timeseries + phase breakdown per route/model, (2) interactive heatmap: token_position x latency bucket (aggregate over window).
- Add tracing span-map to correlate slow traces with heatmap hotspots.
- Design alerts/SLOs that can target phase-specific regressions (e.g., queueing SLO breach).

Definitions / canonical metric names (proposal):
- inference_request_duration_ms_sum, inference_request_duration_ms_count  -- request-level histogram sum/count (ms) with labels: model, model_version, route, deployment, region, priority, rollout_tag
- inference_request_phase_ms_sum, inference_request_phase_ms_count  -- phase-level (phase label = preproc|enqueue|batch_wait|compute|kv_cache|postproc|streaming_flush)
- inference_token_latency_ms_bucket  -- histogram for per-token latency, labels: model, model_version, route, token_position (0-based), token_type (generated|consumed)
- inference_batch_size_distribution_bucket -- histogram for batch sizes (for correlation)
- inference_queue_depth_gauge -- instantaneous queue length by worker/pool
- inference_kv_cache_hit_total, inference_kv_cache_miss_total -- counters for cache behavior
- inference_active_workers_gauge -- pool level active worker count

Label guidance (to avoid high cardinality):
- model and model_version required. route optional (we keep route on by default for product visibility).
- token_position: bucketize at ingestion time into coarse bins for dashboards (e.g., 0-7,8-31,32-127,128-511,512+) OR store exact position but only surface binned positions in the dashboard to avoid cardinality explosion in Prometheus/remote storage.
- rollout_tag: short strings (canary/stable) — max 10 values.
- priority: low|normal|high — avoid freeform values.

Latency "slices" (how we break down request time):
- preproc: request deserialization, validation, routing decisions.
- enqueue: time from handoff to worker queue to being picked (queue wait).
- batch_wait: time waiting for batching window to fill (worker-level).
- compute: GPU time for forward pass (kernel execution).
- kv_cache: explicit time spent looking up/writing KV cache (separate sub-span inside compute).
- postproc: tokenization, output formatting, caller-side framing, streaming flush overhead.
- overhead (non-accounted): IO waits, serialization when not in pre/postproc.

PromQL examples (illustrative) — adjust metric names in exporters:
- Request-level p95 over last 5m: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- Phase breakdown for last 5m (sum of counts per phase): sum(rate(inference_request_phase_ms_sum[5m])) by (phase, route) / sum(rate(inference_request_phase_ms_count[5m])) by (phase, route) 
- Heatmap data series example: sum by (token_position_bucket, le) (rate(inference_token_latency_ms_bucket[5m]))  -- query will need token_position_bucket label created at ingestion time.
- Queueing alert false-positive guard: increase window and compare queue depth with batch_size distribution. Example: avg_over_time(inference_queue_depth_gauge[10m]) > 3 and histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 2000

Heatmap design notes:
- X axis: token_position_bucket (bins: 0-7,8-31,32-127,128-511,512+). Y axis: latency buckets (ms), either plotted as rows of buckets (derived from inference_token_latency_ms_bucket) or as quantile value per position.
- Color: density (requests per bucket) or normalized median/95th per bucket. We should support two modes.
- Time range control: 5m/1h/6h. Default to 15m for interactive use.
- Click-on-cell -> drill to traces and samples (link to trace_id list). Implement a small query service that returns top-N trace_ids for selected token position + latency bucket using label filters.

Tracing/span mapping (proposal):
Span names (convention):
- trace: inference.request (root)
  - inference.preproc
  - inference.enqueue (attributes: queue_id, pool)
  - inference.batch_wait (attributes: batch_target, observed_batch_size)
  - inference.compute (attributes: device, kernel_version, seq_len, kv_cache_used)
    - inference.compute.kv_lookup
    - inference.compute.kernel_exec
  - inference.postproc
  - inference.streaming.flush (if streaming)

Span attributes to include on all spans: model, model_version, route, deployment, region, priority, request_id. Keep attribute keys short but stable.

Trace sampling strategy suggestions:
- Default 1% sampling for all requests, with adaptive sampling to collect more long-tail traces: sample all requests where request_duration > p95 (local recent window) or queue_depth > threshold.
- When a heatmap hotspot is selected (e.g., token bucket X with latency > threshold), enable on-demand higher sampling for 10 minutes for traces that match token_position_bucket=X.

Dashboard layout (wireframe):
Top row: global selectors (time range, model, route, region, deployment, priority, rollout_tag).
Row 1: 3 panel summary: total requests/s, p50/p90/p99 request latency (small sparkline), active workers, queue depth gauge.
Row 2: Latency slices stacked area: time series stacked by phase (preproc/enqueue/batch_wait/compute/postproc) — grouped by route/model selector. Hover shows absolute ms and percent of request.
Row 3: Heatmap panel with token_position_bucket vs latency_buckets. Side panel: toggle color map (density vs p95).
Row 4: Top slow traces table (link to tracing system) and top offending routes/models.
Bottom: supporting panels: batch size distribution, kv cache hit rate, kernel exec time distribution by device.

Alerting / SLO considerations:
- Don't create SLOs on high-cardinality labels (route+model_version can be OK if restricted).
- Phase-specific alert example: If the 99th percentile of enqueue + batch_wait increases by >2x compared to baseline and compute p99 is stable -> page infra/placement team (indicates congestion).
- Use relative-change alerts (week-over-week baseline) with multiple windows to guard against noisy alerts.

Implementation notes & constraints:
- Prometheus remote-write storage (e.g., Cortex/Thanos) required for histograms and long retention. Token_position label is cardinality risk; implement token_position_bucket at exporter level (fast bins) rather than full position label.
- If exporter cannot produce phase-level histograms, we can emit phase duration counters and counts and compute averages in dashboards; histograms are preferred for tails.
- Heatmap queries are heavier; pre-aggregate hourly tiles into a materialized datastore (ClickHouse/BigQuery) for long-range analysis and fast UI. For interactive 15m views, use live Prometheus aggregated query.

Quick prototyping plan:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement phase spans in tracing + exporter changes to emit inference_request_phase_ms_{sum,count} and a simple token_position_bucket label. Wire basic timeseries dashboard with stacked area.
- Phase 2 (3 weeks): add inference_token_latency_ms_bucket histograms, create the heatmap panel and drill-to-trace link logic. Add adaptive sampling hooks.
- Phase 3 (3 weeks): perf optimization: materialize heatmap aggregates in ClickHouse, reduce dashboard query cost, add alerting rules based on slices.

Open questions (to resolve in follow-ups):
- Exact token position bins to use across all models — do we want a single global binning scheme or model-specific? (pros/cons in terms of cardinality and UX).
- Storage: do we accept the extra ingestion volume for token-level histograms or rely on sampled subset? (talk to infra/finance for cost tradeoffs).
- Backfill: do we want to backfill heatmap for past 7 days using existing metrics? Might be lossy if token_position wasn't emitted historically.

Action items / owners:
- (Aisha) Draft exporter changes: list metric names + label semantics -> PR to telemetry repo (due 2024-11-20). JIRA: JIRA-OBS-678.
- (Ethan) Dashboard skeleton in Grafana: stacked-slice panel + placeholder heatmap (due 2024-11-27).
- (Kofi) Trace sampling adaptors: crate rule to upsample traces on p99 breaches (due 2024-12-04).
- (Ruth) Cost estimate: extra series cardinality and storage impact (due 2024-11-18).

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Might integrate a UX control to let SREs toggle token-level telemetry on a per-deployment basis to limit cost for low-value customers.
- Consider a compact 'phase breakdown' tag on request logs so we can crosswalk logs -> traces -> metrics quickly.
- For streaming customers, token_position is moving target; consider 'stream_frame' label for flush boundaries.

References / links:
- CONFLUENCE-OBS-LATENCY-42 (design notes)
- JIRA-OBS-678 (exporter work)
- github: observability PR #452 (prototype dashboard)
